messages:
Sasha: quick favor — seeing a ~15-25% p50 latency regression on serve-2 after the cuBLAS kernel swap. can someone run a short nsys + torch.profiler capture (nvtx + CUDA + host stacks) on a 10-request run so we can get a flamegraph? i'll need cold-start (first request) and steady-state (requests 5-10). upload to s3://redwood-perf/shares/176556/ and scrub any keys. thanks!

Alex: I can take this. ETA ~30m. can you confirm commit + model + seq len and whether to use batch=1?

Sasha: commit: abc1234 (runtime/main), model: redwood/rnnb-2b:v3, seq_len=512, batch=1. run with the current runtime flags we have in perf-qa (no extra quant). prefer CPU host stacks + nvtx markers from our eval harness.

Alex: ok grabbing a p4. proposed nsys cmd (capture ~10 requests):
```
nsys profile --output serve_rnnb_176556 --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none \n  --capture-children=true --force-overwrite true --stats=true --max-size=0 \n  -- python perf_run.py --model redwood/rnnb-2b:v3 --seq 512 --batch 1 --requests 10
```
I'll also run a lightweight torch.profiler inside the harness:
```
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True,
  schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=0, warmup=1, active=4), on_trace_ready=torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler(log_dir)):
  run_inference_loop(10)
```

Alex: will gzip the nsys sqlite if >100MB and upload to s3. I'll add a short README with exact env (CUDA, drivers, runtime commit).

Maria: small tip — set torch.profiler with `use_cuda=True` when using CUDA activities so shapes show up correctly, and include `with record_function('forward'):` around the model step so NVTX maps match. also set `profile_memory=True` to catch any unexpected allocs.

Jonathan: if the nsys trace is huge, run `nsys stats serve_rnnb_176556.qdrep` locally to get kernel hotspots first and attach a flamegraph subset. also please scrub any S3 URIs in the traces that might have creds (we shouldn't have creds in traces but check). ping @sre if we need a temp bucket.

perf-bot: size-check: estimated trace size for 10 steps on RTX6000 ~80-120MB depending on stack depth. recommend `--capture-range=nvtx` and `--max-size=0` to avoid splitting. also recommend `--output-format=sqlite` for easier tooling.

Alex: capture completed and uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/shares/176556/serve_rnnb_176556.qdrep.gz (85MB gz) and torchprof logs in /tmp/176556_torchprof.tar.gz. added README with driver/runtime info and the exact commands I ran. link: https://s3.console.aws/.../serve_rnnb_176556.qdrep.gz

Sasha: got it, thx! quick glance at the flamegraph shows a big chunk in aten::matmul and aten::bmm kernels during linear layers. will run `nsys stats` and post a tiny flame image. if that's the hotspot we may need to revert kernel change or add a cuBLAS config.

Maria: I'll pull the torch.profiler data and compare op-level times. assigning PERF-421 to follow up and add a small micro-benchmark to isolate matmul behavior across kernels.

Jonathan: thanks. once we confirm, we should run a canary on dedicated to validate before any rollback. @sre please standby in case we need capacity or kernel re-deploy windows.

Alex: noted. I left the trace dir with raw qdrep/sqlite and a short script `summarize_trace.sh` that runs `nsys stats --report gputrace` and `python flamegraph_from_nsight.py` so you can re-gen the flame quickly.

Sasha: perfect. i'll post the quick findings in PERF-421 later today. :thumbsup:

Maria: :eyes: I'll follow up on the profiler comparison and post a short notebook with per-op diffs.

perf-bot: reminder: keep thread for async notes — use PERF-421 for long-term tracking.
